name_note: Most genomes GTDB places here carry the NCBI name Enterocloster bolteae; the species was originally described under the name Clostridium bolteae, which the older literature uses.

sentences.text: The species was described from seven obligately anaerobic, gram-positive, rod-shaped, spore-forming organisms isolated from human sources and named Clostridium bolteae.
Strains used carbohydrate as fermentable substrates, producing acetic acid and lactic acid as the major products of glucose metabolism.
C. bolteae and C. clostridioforme prevail in the human intestinal microbiota and are described as opportunistic pathogens with various drug susceptibility patterns.
Genomes of strains isolated from human infection harboured many coding sequences involved in resistance to beta-lactams, glycopeptides, macrolides, aminoglycosides and tetracyclines.
A report describes C. bolteae as overabundant in the intestinal tract of autistic children with gastrointestinal ailments, and found it produces a capsular polysaccharide immunogenic in rabbits.
